extracted.intended_audience: ARIPO search examiners; ARIPO formalities staff; patent applicants and practitioners filing before ARIPO or entering the ARIPO phase under the PCT/Harare Protocol
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for ARIPO examiners and applicants describing (a) what must appear in ARIPO application publications and procedural requirements for PCT entries into the ARIPO phase, and (b) detailed standards, scope and procedures for conducting ARIPO searches and preparing search reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of the publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The publication must contain the description, the claims and any drawings as filed, and specify, where possible, the person(s) designated as the inventor(s). It also indicates the designated Contracting States. The publication also contains any new or amended claims filed by the applicant, together with the ARIPO search report and the abstract determined by the Search Division if available before termination of the technical preparations for publication; otherwise the abstract filed by the applicant is published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the time limit for paying designation fees is still running the publication shows as designated all States party to the Harare Protocol on the date the application was filed; definitive designations (paid) are announced later in the Register and Journal. If a request for correction of errors is allowed it must be incorporated in the publication; if a correction decision is pending on items third parties might take at face value (e.g. priority claims), this must be mentioned on the front page, as must requests for correction and any communication received from the applicant. Further data may be included at the Director General's discretion. The publication may not contain any designation of States finally deemed withdrawn or withdrawn by the applicant before technical preparations for publication end. Originals are used where they meet physical requirements; otherwise amended/replacement documents that meet physical requirements are used. Prohibited material is omitted and the place/number of words or drawings omitted is indicated. Sequence listings filed on date of filing are published as part of the description; those filed later are published as an annex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate publication of the ARIPO search report
rubrics_metrics.description: If not published with the application, the ARIPO search report is published separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search reports that become available after technical preparations for the application publication are to be published on their own; the search opinion itself is not published with the ARIPO search report. Ensure the report is linked to the application for public notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT‑to‑ARIPO phase entry requirements (Rule 23)
rubrics_metrics.description: To initiate the ARIPO phase, requirements for entry into the ARIPO phase according to Rule 23 must be complied with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes timely payment of national/filing and designation fees and provision of translations where required. ARIPO may not process or examine an international application prior to expiry of 31 months from filing (or earliest priority date) unless a specific request is made by the applicant. A copy of the international application is furnished by the IB; translations must be furnished within the specified period or the application is deemed withdrawn (with two-month relief from notification). Check payment and translation requirements when carrying out formal checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing and designation fee deadlines for ARIPO‑PCT applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must pay the filing and designation fees within a period of 21 days from the date of entering the ARIPO phase. Failure to pay in due time means the application is deemed withdrawn; any designation for which the fee has not been paid is deemed withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the ARIPO Office deems the application or a designation withdrawn for failure to pay, it communicates this to the applicant. The loss of rights may be remedied where specified by communications/periods (see translation restoration rules). Ensure fee payments are checked promptly upon entry into the ARIPO phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority document and claim to priority handling
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim to priority for an international application refers to the date(s) claimed under the PCT. Normally the copy of the previous application (priority document) is furnished to ARIPO by the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify priority dates correspond to PCT claim information and that priority documents are obtained or requested when necessary. Treat PCT priority claims in accordance with PCT procedures as applied in ARIPO proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation requirements for PCT/ARIPO applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions of Representation apply to international applications whether furnished in an official language or in translation. A professional representative having a right to practice before the PCT authorities is not necessarily authorized to act before ARIPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether the representative named is authorized to act before ARIPO; invite the applicant to file a separate designation of inventor or representative if required. Do not assume PCT representation suffices for ARIPO procedural steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical requirements and formal examination of international applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must be examined for compliance with the physical requirements. Requirements are generally identical with corresponding PCT requirements and no supplementary examination should be necessary when the application is furnished in an official language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a translation is necessary, the Formality Section must carry out a more extensive formalities examination of that translation. Identify and flag physical defects (see Formal deficiencies criterion) and use originals only if they meet physical requirements otherwise use amended/replacement documents that do comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for grant form equivalence
rubrics_metrics.description: The request for grant for international applications appears on the PCT Request form (Form PCT/RO/101). This corresponds in general to the ARIPO Request for Grant form (Form 3) but may omit certain items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the information supplied on the PCT form corresponds to items ARIPO requires; where items differ follow ARIPO directions and request missing information when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of inventor (naming and timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The designation of inventor must be filed in a separate document where the applicant is not the inventor or the sole inventor, irrespective of the language of the international application, unless the inventor has already been named in the PCT request. Where named in the PCT request the inventor cannot waive his right to be mentioned in the published application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the inventor is not named by 31 months from filing (or earliest priority) ARIPO invites the applicant to file the designation within a specified period. Ensure inventor designation compliance and publish inventor names where required by PCT/ARIPO rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title, drawings and abstract treatment for PCT‑derived applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The title need only meet the less demanding requirements of Rule 5(b). Filing of drawings follows Art.14(2) PCT provisions. The abstract is included in the copy of the international application supplied to ARIPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not subject PCT-conforming titles/drawings/abstracts to unnecessary additional scrutiny beyond what PCT and Harare Protocol require, except when translation issues or other deviations occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional application timing and language requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: One or more ARIPO divisional applications may be filed in respect of subject‑matter contained in an earlier ARIPO‑PCT application but not before the latter application is pending before ARIPO (i.e. has entered ARIPO phase). The divisional must be filed in the language of the earlier application if that language is an official ARIPO language; otherwise in the language of the translation furnished to ARIPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify pendency before allowing divisionals and ensure language compliance with ARIPO official languages or provided translation. Treat divisional filings with the same physical/formality checks as main applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing filing and publication rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules 5.2 and 13ter PCT apply to filing of sequence listings. Sequence listings filed on date of filing are published as part of the description; those filed later are published as an annex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure correct format (paper/electronic), timing, and placement in publication or annex as per filing date. Omit or flag prohibited material in sequence listings before publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective of the search
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective of the search is to discover the prior art which is relevant for the purpose of determining whether, and if so to what extent, the invention to which the application relates is new and involves an inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Searchers should focus on locating relevant prior art that could affect novelty or inventive step and provide a reasoned opinion in the search report; decisions on novelty and inventive step remain for the Substantive Examiner but the search opinion should enable applicant reply and inform examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search documentation to be consulted
rubrics_metrics.description: Search is carried out through consultation of internal or external collections or databases systematically accessible (words, classification symbols, indexing codes). These are primarily patent documents, supplemented by articles from periodicals and other non‑patent literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure coverage of core patent literature and appropriate non‑patent sources; follow PCT minimum documentation (Rule 34 PCT) and extend where ARIPO‑specific or field‑specific sources justify it (see Special documents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and completeness of the search
rubrics_metrics.description: The ARIPO search is essentially a thorough, high‑quality, all‑embracing search but 100% completeness cannot always be obtained. The search should be carried out to reduce to a minimum the possibility of failing to discover complete anticipations for any claims or other highly relevant prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept lower recall for less relevant prior art; use examiner judgement and available facilities to approximate the scope of an International search. Consult PCT‑specified documentation and use available resources efficiently while aiming to find highly relevant anticipations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness and efficiency of the search (use of order and strategy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effectiveness and efficiency depend on the degree of order available in the collection: words, classification units, indexing codes, bibliographical links. The examiner should exercise judgement, based on knowledge of technology and retrieval systems, to omit sections where likelihood of finding relevant documents is negligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create or use search strategies to focus on likely sections; omit material such as documents from periods before the field developed; consult only one patent family member unless substantial content differences are suspected. Balance thoroughness with economic/time constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special documents beyond PCT minimum to consult for ARIPO searches
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain categories of documents may be of special relevance to the ARIPO patent system though not part of the PCT minimum documentation; these should be consulted for ARIPO searches, additional searches, and international‑type searches, and for national searches unless excluded by agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify regionally or technically important literature, databases, or non‑patent sources relevant to Contracting States and include them when warranted. Document which special sources were consulted in the search report where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search in analogous technical fields
rubrics_metrics.description: The search strategy should cover directly relevant technical fields and may need to be extended to analogous fields; the need must be judged in each case by the examiner, taking into account the outcome of the initial search sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider which fields are analogous based on the essential technical contribution of the invention, not merely stated functions. Extend the search to analogous fields when it is probable that a reasonable objection of lack of inventive step could be established from what is likely to be found there. Do not try to imagine all possible applications as an inventor would.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet searches and online sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The ARIPO search can cover internet sources, including online technical journals, databases or other websites. The extent depends on the case; in some technical fields a systematic internet search will regularly be necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In information/software fields internet searches may be essential; carefully document internet searches and sources. Use internet searches to supplement database collections where they are likely to reveal relevant prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for the search (claims as starting point)
rubrics_metrics.description: The search should be made on the basis of the claims, with due regard to the description and drawings. The claims determine the extent of the protection which will be conferred if a patent is granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyse claims to identify the subject‑matter to be searched but consult description/drawings for essential features and examples; include features indicated in the description as essential even if not literally in the claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of claims for the search
rubrics_metrics.description: The search should not be restricted to the literal wording of the claims, nor broadened to include everything derivable by a person skilled in the art from the description. It should be directed to essential features and take into account changes in the objective technical problem occurring during the search; consider well‑known equivalents to claim features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Searchers should balance literal and purposive interpretation: include equivalents and commonly known variants that may undermine inventive step, but avoid undue enlargement beyond what is supported. Claims referencing description parts (allowed only where 'absolutely necessary') should still be searched if technical features are unambiguously defined there.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of amended claims and basis for supplementary search
rubrics_metrics.description: The search and examination is directed to the claims as originally filed or amended in the ARIPO application. For ARIPO‑PCT applications the applicant may enter ARIPO with amendments made in the international phase; ARIPO gives the applicant opportunity to amend within a set time limit. The application as amended serves as the basis for any supplementary ARIPO search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When amendments occur before the ARIPO search, perform supplementary searches to cover amended subject‑matter; when amendments derive from the international phase ensure the ARIPO phase includes the intended set of claims. Communicate new documents found in any additional search to the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of abandoned claims from the search
rubrics_metrics.description: For ARIPO applications, claims that are deemed to have been abandoned for non‑payment of fees must be excluded from the search. This applies to directly‑filed ARIPO applications and supplementary ARIPO searches for ARIPO‑PCT applications entering the ARIPO phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify fee payment status and exclude abandoned claims from search scope. If a claim has been abandoned but later restored, confirm timelines and whether a supplementary search is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipation of possible amendments to claims during search
rubrics_metrics.description: Insofar as possible and reasonable, the search should cover the entire subject‑matter to which the claims are directed or to which they might reasonably be expected to be directed after amendment (e.g., include detailed embodiments shown in description even if claims are functional only).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When claims are functional or broad but the description contains detailed non‑trivial examples, include those examples in the search. Aim to anticipate reasonable claim amendments that applicants may make and search accordingly, within reason and resource limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of unduly broad or speculative claims (Rule 7(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: No special search effort need be made for searching unduly wide or speculative claims beyond the extent to which they relate to matter sufficiently disclosed in the application and supported by the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not extend the search to unrelated fields merely because of broad wording unless it's probable such an extended search could produce documents enabling a reasonable objection for lack of novelty/inventive step. If the disclosure is too deficient to enable a meaningful search over the whole claimed scope consider an incomplete search or declaration taking place of a search report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search approach for independent and dependent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections consulted for searching the independent claim(s) must include all dependent claims. Dependent claims should be interpreted as restricted by all features of the claims upon which they depend. If the independent claim is found novel by the search, there is generally no need to make further search or cite documents for dependent claims as such.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search dependent claims within the same sections used for the independent claim; when the independent claim's patentability is questioned, assess dependent claims further where necessary, but avoid redundant searching when independent claim stands. Use examples in text to guide limits of extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search on dependent claims when independent claim is challenged
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the patentability of the independent claim is questioned it may be necessary to continue the search for the dependent claim in other sections to assess whether the dependent claim as such is novel and involves an inventive step. No special search should be made for trivial or generally known features, though quickly found handbooks showing general knowledge should be cited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extend search to additional classification units when dependent claims add meaningful technical features potentially distinguishing over cited prior art. Cite general reference works rapidly if they establish that features are known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search for combinations and sub‑combinations of elements
rubrics_metrics.description: For claims characterized by a combination of elements the search should be directed towards the combination; when searching the sections for this purpose, sub‑combinations and individual elements should be searched in those sections at the same time. Additional sections for sub‑combinations/individual elements should be searched only if necessary to establish novelty for assessing inventive step of the combination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search both the full combination and relevant sub‑combinations in the initial sections consulted; only expand to other units if needed to determine novelty/inventive step. Ensure documentation of which sub‑combinations were considered and why further search was or was not necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of different claim categories in the search
rubrics_metrics.description: When the application contains claims of different categories, all these must be included in the search. However, if a product claim clearly seems both new and non‑obvious, the examiner should make no special effort to search claims for a process which inevitably results in manufacture of that product or for use of the product. When an application contains only one category it may be desirable to include others in the search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include product/process/use claims as appropriate but use pragmatic judgment: e.g., starting products in chemical process claims may be assumed part of the prior art and need not be searched unless indicated otherwise. Document scope decisions in the search report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject‑matter excluded from the search
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may exclude certain subject‑matter from his search where it does not comply with Harare Protocol provisions or national laws relating to exclusions from patentability or where the application fails to comply to such extent that a meaningful search is impossible for some/all claims, or where Rule 7 bis.3 issues arise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify exclusions (e.g., non‑patentable subject matter or lack of industrial applicability) and notify the applicant where search restriction is applied. Consider incomplete search or declaration where meaningful search cannot be done due to lack of compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of unity and restriction of search
rubrics_metrics.description: When the claims do not relate to one invention only or to a group of inventions linked by a single general inventive concept, the search will normally be restricted to the invention or linked group first mentioned in the claims. Restriction is notified to the applicant in a communication with the partial search report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply lack‑of‑unity rules consistently; prepare partial search report and communicate the restriction grounds and whether additional searches can be requested and on what basis. Ensure applicant is informed of consequences for examination and fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Including technological background in the search
rubrics_metrics.description: In certain circumstances it may be desirable to extend the search to include the 'technological background' of the invention: preamble to the first claim, state of the art mentioned in the description introduction, and the general technological background of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extend searches to background material when it helps assess novelty and inventive step, particularly where background may contain anticipatory or analogous disclosures. Document reasons for including background materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure prior to searching — analysis of the application
rubrics_metrics.description: When taking up an application to be searched the examiner should first consider the application to determine the subject of the claimed invention: make a critical analysis of the claims in light of the description and drawings to identify the problem, the inventive concept, essential features to the solution, and results and effects obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include technical features not in claims if description indicates they are essential; identify search keywords, classification units and strategy based on this analysis. Use this analysis to prioritize sections and resources for the search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling formal deficiencies observed during search
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner notices formal shortcomings overlooked by the Formality Section he calls these to the attention of the Formality Section by internal communication but should not repeat the tasks of the Formality Section or undertake time‑consuming enquiries into these matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of formal deficiencies include: no paper and/or no electronic sequence listing; incorrect sequence/positioning of page numbering or failure to use Arabic numerals; presence of drawings in the description and/or claims. Flag such issues internally and continue substantive search work without duplicating formality checks.
